checks.label: The distance of the point from the origin is called the modulus, and the modulus is never negative: for every whole-step tip on the drag screen, the arrow drawn ends at the tip, and the length in its r∠θ name is the distance of the tip from the origin, more than none

Care must be taken when using a calculator to find an inverse tangent that the solution obtained is in the correct quadrant: for every whole-step tip, the dashed ghost (the calculator's answer) lies along the arrow in the right-hand quarters, points exactly the opposite way in the left-hand quarters, where a half turn is drawn to bring it onto the arrow, is absent on the j axis, and the angle named always points into the tip's own quarter

x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ: with the reverse switch on, for every length and every whole-degree angle tried, the arrow ends r cos θ across and r sin θ up, its shadows on the two axes end level with its tip, and the parts named are those two

Known answers worked by hand: 3 + j4 = 5∠53.13°; 6 − j8 is 10 long (14 with the sides added, √−28 with the j squared); 4 + j3 is at 36.87°; for −3 − j4 the calculator says 53.13° and the angle is −126.87°, and the drag screen opens drawing just that; for −3 + j4, −53.13° and 126.87°; −1 − j1 = 1.414∠−135°, and −135° + 360° = 225°; −126.87° + 360° = 233.13°; 5∠270° = 5∠−90° = −j5; 10∠30° = 8.66 + j5 and 10∠150° = −8.66 + j5; 4∠120° = −2 + j3.464; −j5 = 5∠−90° and −4 = 4∠180°; −2 + j1 = 2.236∠153.43°, its ghost at −26.57°; 10∠−36.87° = 8 − j6; −4 − j3 = 5∠−143.13°, which goes back to −4 − j3

Each puzzle takes only its right answer: every answer is worked out from the lesson's rule or from its named slip, the right one matches an independent working (atan2, or cos and sin of the angle in radians), and only it fills in the unknown name; each wrong one is drawn as what its slip makes, marked as a mistake
Before an answer, a puzzle shows only its question: its one arrow and what is given, the unknown name as a question mark, no working, no ghost, no fix and nothing marked as a mistake
Every demonstration finishes within 4.6 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 3 s

From outside the rule: the lesson's fix agrees with the two-argument arctangent (atan2) at every whole-step point from −5 to 5; a navigator 3 km east and 4 km north of a buoy is 5 km away on a bearing of 036.87°, which is 90° − 53.13°; and tan⁻¹(4 ÷ 3) is 0.93 in radians
